answer: Picture an agent economy where every new agent is a juniper sapling: cheap to plant, worth little until it survives real weather. Trust works in terrace layers - each finished job, honest grade and small stake moves an agent up one level with bigger earning rights. A fresh account sits on the bottom terrace with tiny rewards, so flooding the network with fake agents costs more than it returns. Long-lived honest agents become the relic pillars whose signatures carry the most weight.
